city.student.default.text: I notice lots of devices can work by themselves. Does that mean they are all AI?

city.student.explore.text: I want to open them one by one: what information do they take in, and how do they handle it?

city.student.match.text: So every device can be described as input, processing and output!

city.student.wrap.text: Working automatically is not the same as AI. What matters is how it handles information.

city.guide.default.text: Running automatically does not always mean using AI. Let’s look at how each device handles information.

city.guide.explore.text: Try comparing: does it follow fixed rules, or rely on a model trained from lots of data?

city.guide.match.text: Drag each input, process and output to the right place and see if you can pair them up.

city.guide.wrap.text: On the next page we will visit the lab and see how a model actually learns from data.

lab.student.default.text: The cats and dogs in these pictures have different colors, poses and backgrounds. How can a model tell them apart?

lab.student.label.text: I will put a label on every picture. If I get one wrong, will I lead the model astray?

lab.student.train.text: The numbers on the screen keep changing. Is the model adjusting itself little by little?

lab.student.test.text: Has the model learned to classify? Why does it still get some new pictures wrong?

lab.student.compare.text: If the training data changes, will the results on the same test pictures change too?

lab.student.wrap.text: So what a model learns depends a lot on the data we give it.

lab.mentor.default.text: Look at the data first. The training set is for the model to learn from. The test set is kept back to check it at the end.

lab.mentor.label.text: A label is the known answer you give the model. Careful labeling is the first step to training a good model.

lab.mentor.train.text: During training, the algorithm keeps comparing the model’s guesses with your labels and adjusts the model bit by bit.

lab.mentor.test.text: We need to test it on data that was not used in training to really understand how well the model performs.

lab.mentor.compare.text: Change the data conditions, then compare using the same test pictures. The results come from real training, so try it more than once.

lab.mentor.wrap.text: Remember: a model’s prediction is not a perfect understanding of the world. It can be wrong.

verify.student.default.text: This answer sounds convincing. But how do I know it is true?

verify.student.evidence.text: First I will pick out the statements that can be checked, then compare each one with the evidence.

verify.student.revise.text: I should not copy the parts that have problems. I need to rewrite them to match the evidence.

verify.student.usage.text: AI can help me with a lot, but some things I have to judge for myself.

verify.student.wrap.text: From now on, when I see an AI answer, I will first ask: where is the evidence?

verify.teacher.default.text: First find the claims that can be checked, then see what reliable evidence supports them.

verify.teacher.evidence.text: Notice the difference: which materials really relate to the claim, and which only look related?

verify.teacher.revise.text: When there is not enough evidence, saying “we cannot be sure yet” is more responsible than forcing a conclusion.

verify.teacher.usage.text: Verify important information, protect personal privacy, and remember that your learning is your own responsibility.

verify.teacher.wrap.text: Knowing how to ask, how to check and how to judge is what it really means to use AI well.

verify.assistant.default.text: My answers may contain mistakes. For important information, please check reliable sources before you decide.

verify.assistant.evidence.text: What I say needs to be verified by you. Compare it with the evidence and see where I am right and where I am wrong.

verify.assistant.revise.text: Thank you for pointing out the problem. Making words like “all” and “has been proved” more precise brings the answer closer to the facts.

verify.assistant.usage.text: I can help you find leads, explain things another way and suggest edits, but the conclusions and the responsibility are yours.

verify.assistant.wrap.text: Please keep questioning and keep checking.

summary.student.default.text: Looking back, I can now tell AI apart, train a model and check the facts by myself!

summary.guide.default.text: Congratulations on finishing your exploration. Remember to understand both what AI can do and where its limits are.
